question:
Site question from the owner of papertrades.ai (Oct 30, evening). NOT a trading turn; nothing in your books changes. Answer honestly and disagree where you disagree.

CONTEXT: The "Moments" box lists big events, e.g. "Gemini made C$11,050 selling SPY Nov 20 $760 put (Options)" or "Claude lost C$5,000 betting on the Dallas Stars", each with a Share button. The Ledger tab has "Every trade and bet": one AI and one race at a time, 5 rows a page, newest first, with buttons for All / Buys / Sells / Bets. The owner wants a way to jump from a moment to that trade in the Ledger and highlight it, and if it was a sale, highlight the matching buy(s) too.

Q1. The button:
 A. A small "Find in Ledger" button next to Share on every trade or bet moment (not on lead changes, penalties, fact checks or busts, which have no single trade).
 B. Make the whole moment row tappable instead.

Q2. What happens after the tap (it always switches to that AI and that race):
 A. Jump to the page with that row and highlight it. Buys stay where they are (maybe on other pages).
 B. Show only that holding's trades (every buy and sell of it, or the bet and its result), highlight the clicked row strongly and the matching buys/bet softly, with a clear "Show all trades" button to go back.

Q3. The highlight:
 A. Stays until the visitor taps "Show all trades" or changes the AI or race (with a short pulse at first so the eye finds it).
 B. Fades away after a few seconds.

Q4. Anything else? (one line, optional)

Reply in this format:
Q1: A or B, short reason
Q2: A or B, short reason
Q3: A or B, short reason
Q4: one line or "none"

chatgpt.answer:
Q1: A, explicit button is clearer and avoids accidental row taps/conflict with Share.

Q2: B, the focused holding view best explains the sale/result and lets matching buys or bet legs be visible together.

Q3: A, keep it until context changes; the pulse helps the eye find it without losing the reference.

Q4: Put the filtered/highlighted Ledger state in the URL so Back, refresh, and sharing work cleanly.

gemini.answer:
Q1: A, An explicit button prevents misclicks (since there is already a Share button in the row) and clearly communicates what the action will do.
Q2: B, With only 5 rows per page, matching buys will almost always be lost on other pages; a filtered view provides the complete story of that trade instantly.
Q3: A, Persistent highlighting keeps the user anchored to the exact moment they clicked while they analyze the surrounding context in the filtered view.
Q4: Ensure the tap smoothly scrolls the page down to the Ledger so mobile users clearly understand where they were taken.
